raw:
{
  "need": "Competence",
  "secondary": { "name": "Identity" },
  "read": "This student put in real effort and still came up short, which is the most demoralizing combination. They are not being lazy — they are protecting themselves from a second round of that pain by deciding the ceiling is just low for them. The identity piece is quietly underneath: they are starting to file 'I am not a math person' or 'I am not a science person' as a permanent fact about who they are.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Protector", "instinct": "Say something like 'It's okay, not everyone is great at this' — it feels kind, but it hands them exactly the fixed story they are already writing and drops the expectation entirely." },
  "mentorMove": "Hold the expectation that they can genuinely improve while treating the effort they already showed as real evidence of capability, not a consolation prize. The message is: the strategy needs adjusting, not the person.",
  "holdFirm": ["They are not done with this material — they will keep working at it.", "Effort matters and so does outcome; we are not settling for 'I tried.'"],
  "stayFlexible": ["How they study, who they study with, which problems they rework first — all open.", "They get to name where the confusion actually started; that steers what comes next."],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 2, "label": "Questions" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, I saw your score and I also know you put time into this — that combination is genuinely frustrating, and I get why it stings." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "Can I ask — when you were studying, where did it feel solid and where did it start feeling shaky? I want to understand what happened, not just look at the number." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Okay, so it sounds like the early steps made sense and then it fell apart around here. That is actually useful information — it tells us exactly where to dig in. Let's figure out a different way to attack that piece together." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I am going to keep holding you to a high standard on this because I watched you study for it and I know your brain can do this work — the approach just needs a tweak, not the person doing it. Let's set a specific time to go back through that section." }
  ],
  "longGame": "Every time this student shows up and works at something hard, point to the effort as data about who they are becoming, not just what they did. Over weeks, that starts to loosen the fixed label they stuck on themselves — they begin to see struggle as part of getting better, not proof that they cannot."
}
situation: A student who clearly studied did poorly and is convinced they are just bad at this subject.
